title: Can remote work save small towns?
title_es: ¿Puede el trabajo remoto salvar a los pueblos?

task: ¿Te mudarías a un pueblo si pudieras trabajar a distancia? Escribe 130–160 palabras con ventajas, desventajas y una conclusión, usando conectores como nevertheless, moreover y on the whole.
paragraphs: For decades, the story of rural areas in many countries has been one of decline. Young people left for the cities in search of jobs, schools closed, and shops pulled down their shutters for the last time. Then, almost overnight, the pandemic changed the rules. Millions of office workers discovered that they could do their jobs from a kitchen table, and some began to wonder why that table had to be in an expensive city.

Some towns were quick to seize the opportunity. Since 2018, a programme in Tulsa, Oklahoma, has offered remote workers ten thousand dollars to relocate there for at least a year. Villages in Spain, Italy and Ireland have set up co-working spaces in old schools and post offices, sometimes combined with cheap housing, in the hope of attracting new residents.

Supporters argue that the benefits go well beyond the newcomers themselves. Remote workers earn city salaries but spend their money locally, in cafés, shops and gyms. Their children keep schools open, and their presence can make it worthwhile for businesses to stay. Some studies of relocation programmes suggest that most participants remain in their new home after the incentive ends.

Nevertheless, the picture is not entirely rosy. Fast and reliable internet is still a luxury in many rural areas, and without it the whole idea collapses. Moreover, the arrival of well-paid outsiders can push up house prices, making it harder for local young people to stay. In some popular villages, long-standing residents complain that they are becoming strangers in their own streets.

There is also the question of whether remote work is here to stay. Since the pandemic ended, many large companies have called their employees back to the office for at least part of the week, which makes living hundreds of kilometres away far less practical.

Perhaps the most realistic conclusion is that remote work will not reverse rural decline on its own, but it can be one tool among many. Towns that combine good connections with affordable housing, decent services and a genuine welcome for newcomers seem to have the best chance of turning a temporary trend into a lasting revival.
